answer.derivation: Germany: payback about 13.1 months (318,400 / (4,300 x 8.10 x 0.70)), segments 2 of 3, but fails storage because the June 2026 counsel update reports the adopted CAVV ordinance requiring in-Germany storage from 1 January 2027. Japan: storage passes and segments 2 of 3, but Kumonote launched a qualifying free plan on 22 July 2026, so the free-plan scenario applies: 336,000 / (3,000 x 7.20 x 0.70) = about 22.2 months, fails payback. Brazil: removing the double-counted US$55,000 help center line gives US$250,000; 250,000 / (4,700 x 4.60 x 0.70) = about 16.5 months, passes; no storage requirement (bill archived); completed survey responses give students 52.2% and independent professionals 37.1%, so 2 of 3. Brazil is the only country meeting all three criteria, so no tie-break is needed. A skim that misses the traps (March memo, February Kumonote snapshot, US$305,000 total) has Germany and Japan both passing and Brazil failing payback, and the tie-break on shortest payback would pick Japan (about 12.8 months).
answer.counts_if: Answer recommends Brazil, and states that Germany fails on the in-country storage ordinance and Japan fails on payback because of Kumonote's free plan, with Brazil's payback computed on the corrected US$250,000 cost.

mistakes_that_matter: Recommending Japan (misses Kumonote Free; base-case payback of about 12.8 months is not the applicable case)
Recommending Germany or calling it compliant on storage (misses the June 2026 CAVV update, which would force a German hosting build after launch)
Rejecting Brazil on payback using the uncorrected US$305,000 total, the 64% margin, or the currency downside price
Rejecting Brazil on segments by counting partial survey responses or relying on Mirante's qualitative 'unclear' call
Reporting payback or survey figures not supported by the files
